craft.title: A new board, *every month*
craft.text: Each month the group booked the same boards across Belgrade and changed the message: pre-enrolment, a new course, a spring intake, a programme for career changers. The red and the two crests stay, so a driver knows the school before reading a word. Every board went to print in 8×3, 4×3 and 5×2.6 metres, with a LED animation and a social set.

craft.text: Between two billboards the college still has news every week: pass rates, competitions, study programmes, a freshers’ party. craft.text: A high school talks to teenagers and to their parents at once. Student apps get the app’s own colours, school trips get boarding passes and pins on a map, an anniversary gets a candle on a cake. The red and the crest hold it together.

craft.title: Twenty years, *twenty* prizes
craft.text: ITS turned twenty, so the enrolment offer became twenty jubilee packages: the lowest fees of the year plus tech or sports gear. A giant 20 carries the headphones, the sneakers and the price, and the gift box comes back as a printed voucher with a satin ribbon. One key visual, every format in the same week.

craft.title: First, open *the door*
craft.text: The year starts with one question: why here? FSU Doors answers in three posts, “Create it. Move it. What did you open?”, that work alone and read as one campaign in the grid. The same promise then travels to direct entry without an exam, the first-stroke series and the printed flyer.

craft.title: Then pay for *the reach*
craft.text: The campaigns that carry enrolment run as paid ads on Instagram and Facebook, so each one is built four times: story 9:16, feed 4:5, square and link 1.91:1. Every format is laid out again from the same picture, with the type inside Meta’s safe zones, never a crop of the square.

craft.title: One frame, *thirty-eight courses*
craft.text: Then every programme has to explain itself, course by course. Contemporary Design MA: 38 posts where a pencil sketch turns into the finished space, each with its own accent colour. Costume Design MA keeps the frame and changes the costume, so a long series never feels like one post repeated.

craft.title: Then fill *the building*
craft.text: A school is also its nights and its Saturdays. The freshers’ party, painting under UV light, free workshops for teenagers and a Halloween corner each get their own mood, and the open calls that take students to bigger stages are staged as objects, not announcements.

craft.title: And tell *everyone*
craft.text: News posts are where a school’s feed usually goes grey. Here the headline lives inside the picture: a quote tucked behind her hair, “Hollywood” stacked behind his books, a name painted on a wall in Užice. Even a calendar day gets an idea: light through a prism, four ways to draw one head.

craft.title: Ten programmes, *every format*
craft.text: Each study programme gets one cinematic signature, then the grid rebuilds it for story, feed and website without losing the picture.

craft.title: 117 slides that *teach*
craft.text: ChatGPT Commands: nine carousels, one prompt per slide. A strict type system keeps long, practical text calm enough to read in a feed.

craft.title: One campaign, *four formats*
craft.text: ITS advertises on Instagram and Facebook all year. Ten study programmes each get their own face and their own set of story, feed, square and link formats; pre-enrolment, the 20-year jubilee packages and Black Friday run on the same system. Every format is laid out again inside Meta’s safe zones, never cropped from the square.

craft.title: A number you can *walk around*
craft.text: Between the series, ITS news gets one idea per post. Pass rates are built as objects in the scene: a 3D ring around the student, vinyl on a glass wall, digits behind an exploded camera, a red 100% standing on the floor. The same thinking carries the calendar days and the open calls.

craft.title: A high school with *its own voice*
craft.text: ITHS speaks to fifteen-year-olds and to their parents, so every post starts from a line they would repeat: “School ends at 14:30. That’s it. Really.” A former pupil comes back as a teacher on a red-pen worksheet, a poetry contest is written in a journal, a charity tournament is painted on the court.

craft.title: Product-true, *frame by frame*
